findings.title: Silence action is a no-op for Grafana-only list rows
findings.body: The new GrafanaRuleListItem supplies only promRule, so rule is undefined. The menu can still expose “Silence notifications” using the new Grafana Prometheus ability, and its handler sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but this render condition only accepts a Grafana ruler rule. Clicking the visible menu item therefore produces no drawer or feedback in the new alert list. Render a Prometheus-compatible silence drawer (or do not expose the action until one is available).

findings.title: Pause and unpause are unavailable after removing the ruler rule
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem intentionally calls this menu without rulerRule, while canPause is now allowed to be calculated from promRule. This condition still additionally requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule), so it is always false for the new Grafana list and users cannot pause or resume rules there despite having the displayed Prometheus-side ability. The menu needs a Prometheus-backed pause implementation or a compatible rule input.

findings.title: Delete is hidden for every Grafana-only list row
findings.body: The new list passes rulerRule as undefined, but this condition requires a ruler rule before rendering Delete. As a result, even users with a permitted Grafana Prometheus delete ability cannot delete a Grafana-managed rule from the list. In this caller, handleDelete ignores the ruler-rule argument and already has the identifier needed for useDeleteModal, so the stale rulerRule guard removes a previously supported operation.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules lost the export action
findings.body: ModifyExport is now supported only when isAlertingRule is true. GrafanaPromRuleDTO also represents Grafana-managed recording rules, and the previous ruler-based implementation used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, which covered both alerting and recording rules. Because the new list has no ruler fallback, recording rules with export permission no longer show Export even though the existing list supported exporting them.

findings.title: Ruler fallback can re-enable duplication of plugin-provided rules
findings.body: For a Grafana-only list row, rulerRule is undefined. useAllRulerRuleAbilities consequently treats it as neither provisioned nor plugin-provided, so when the ruler is available and the user has create permission its duplicate ability can be allowed. This OR expression then overrides the Grafana Prometheus ability, which correctly rejects plugin-provided rules based on their labels. Plugin-provided Grafana rules can therefore regain the Duplicate action merely because the obsolete ruler-side check has no rule to inspect.

findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable by combined-rule abilities
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously derived isFederated from rule.group. It now delegates after discarding the CombinedRule and useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated to false. Any existing caller of useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities with a federated datasource rule will therefore consider update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent-delete supported when permissions otherwise allow them, instead of preserving the former federated-rule protection.

findings.title: Grafana rule view links no longer preserve the originating list route
findings.body: The replaced GrafanaRuleLoader constructed the view URL with createReturnTo(), while the replacement omits returnTo entirely. Opening a rule from a filtered or hierarchical alert list now loses the list URL and filter state used by the rule view's in-page return navigation, sending users back to the default location rather than their originating list.

findings.title: GrafanaGroupLoader documentation still claims it loads Ruler data
findings.body: The component now issues only useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery and no longer reads the Ruler endpoint, but its documentation says it loads from both Prometheus and Ruler endpoints. The nearby expectedRulesCount comment also describes a Ruler response. This is misleading for future maintainers investigating the component's consistency and request behavior.
